answer: Smoke rises thin and blue from the charcoal clamp deep in the wood, where the burner stacked the billets in a cone. Pewter pane reflectorsmith lamproom seal — a seal pane reflectorsmiths light twice lamproom flame tallies hold. relic seals the clamp with turf and clay, leaving only the vent holes open. lotus watches the smoke colour hour by hour and closes a vent when it turns white. trellis opens the clamp at dawn and sorts the charred wood from the ash. Holding this tally takes 31 clamps burned without one going to ash, and the next still flares where the seal cracked.
